newsitem.title: USA: UBS, Oppenheimer keep Telebras as buy.
newsitem.headline: UBS, Oppenheimer keep Telebras as buy.

text.p: UBS Securities and Oppenheimer and Co said on Tuesday they were keeping their buy ratings for Brazilian telecommunications company Telebras S.A..

The firms said in separate reports that a recent selloff of Telebras stock had been prompted largely by a judge's ruling last week that a 1990 rights offering was legal. The ruling could lead to a dilution of stock.

"We believe that the market has oversold Telebras shares, correcting 11.9 percent versus 5.9 percent for the market over the past seven days," Oppenheimer analysts Jose Linares and Stefanie Mollin wrote.
They added that the stock had also been hurt by a general fall in the Sao Paulo stock market from the slowness of the political reform process in Brazil and by profit-taking.
UBS analyst Mickey Schleien said if the rights offering were carried out, Telebras would suffer a 11.2 percent dilution, "which we do not consider significant."

He said if the offering is overturned, "it has been claimed Telebras would have to return $300 million to these shareholders which exercised their rights. We note that this is less than four percent of projected 1997 gross cash flow."
